introduction: Each workspace's repository is held durably in Cloudflare Artifacts, copied in from the forge with the workspace's own credential and reached through one platform interface. This package also establishes, by exercising them, the three store capabilities the contract needs and the documentation does not describe.

glossary.copy-in: Bringing the repository at a workspace's git_url into the workspace's repository, with the workspace's credential where it has one, as the initial clone and as the mechanism every later sync reuses.
glossary.origin credential: The credential for a workspace's own remote, resolved from the workspace secrets GIT_PAT, else GIT_USERNAME with GIT_PASSWORD, else none.
glossary.repository store: The platform interface through which the service creates, reads, writes and removes a workspace's repository. Its Cloudflare implementation is Cloudflare Artifacts.
glossary.store capability: One of the three behaviours the contract needs and the store's documentation does not describe: refs outside refs/heads/ and refs/tags/, a non-fast-forward update, and a ref deletion.
glossary.upstream credential: The credential for a carry_patch workspace's upstream, resolved from UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT, else UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME with UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD, else the origin credential.

requirements.title: One durable repository per workspace
requirements.rationale: Every later package addresses a workspace's repository, so the mapping and its durability have to be unambiguous before anything is built on them.

criteria.action: address each workspace's repository by a name derived from the workspace's slug and the short hash of its id, so the mapping needs no separate record
criteria.contract: for a given workspace the same repository name is computed on every call; two workspaces never compute the same name; the name holds only characters the store accepts

criteria.action: create its repository in the store
criteria.contract: the store holds a repository under the workspace's derived name immediately after the create route answers

criteria.action: keep a repository and its refs across the restart or eviction of every other component of the deployment
criteria.contract: refs and objects written before a restart are readable after it, with no re-copy

criteria.action: take the workspace lock around every operation that writes a workspace's repository
criteria.contract: for any two concurrent writing operations on one workspace, one completes before the other begins, and the second answers 409 workspace_busy when it may not wait

requirements.title: Copying a repository in
requirements.rationale: A private repository is the ordinary case, and the store's own import cannot carry a credential, so this path carries almost every workspace.

criteria.condition: a workspace is created with a valid body
criteria.action: copy the repository at git_url into the workspace's repository, bringing every branch and tag
criteria.contract: once the copy completes, every branch and tag of the remote is present in the workspace's repository at the same commit

criteria.guard: the workspace has a stored origin credential
criteria.action: authenticate to the remote with that credential
criteria.contract: a private remote is copied successfully; the credential appears in no response body and no log record

criteria.guard: the workspace has no stored origin credential
criteria.action: copy from the remote without authenticating
criteria.contract: a public remote is copied successfully with no credential; a private one fails and is reported as a failed copy

criteria.condition: the credentials given on create are refused by the remote with an authentication failure
criteria.action: refuse the create before any workspace is written
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; no workspace row, no secret and no repository exists afterwards; a remote that is unreachable, that fails or that does not answer is not refused this way but answers 201 and fails the copy

criteria.condition: a copy fails after the workspace was created, whether from the network, a refusal by the remote or a remote that does not exist
criteria.action: leave the workspace readable with status failed and the reason recorded
criteria.contract: the workspace's status is "failed" and clone_error names the failure; the workspace is still readable and can be archived or recloned; no credential appears in clone_error

criteria.condition: a copy cannot finish within one unit of platform work
criteria.action: continue it in another, resuming at the first ref it has not yet brought across
criteria.contract: a repository larger than one unit of work can transfer reaches status ready with every branch present, and the refs an earlier unit brought across are not transferred again

requirements.title: Clone status
requirements.rationale: status and clone_error are what every client polls, and a workspace stuck in cloning is one nobody can use or recover.

criteria.action: move a workspace's status from pending to cloning and then to ready or failed, and set head_sha from the repository's HEAD once it is ready
criteria.contract: the observed sequence of statuses is a prefix of pending, cloning, ready or pending, cloning, failed; head_sha is a 40-character hex string when the status is ready and null before

criteria.condition: a workspace has been in status cloning for 30 minutes
criteria.action: move it to failed and record why
criteria.contract: the workspace's status is "failed" with clone_error set; no workspace remains in cloning indefinitely

criteria.guard: its repository was kept when it was archived
criteria.action: reuse the kept repository rather than copying from the remote again
criteria.contract: the workspace reaches ready without a transfer from the remote, and commits present only in the kept repository are still present

requirements.title: What the store really does with refs
requirements.rationale: Three capabilities the contract needs are undocumented, and three later packages are designed differently depending on the answer.

criteria.action: declare whether it accepts a ref outside refs/heads/ and refs/tags/, a non-fast-forward update of a ref, and the deletion of a ref, and be held to that declaration against a real store
criteria.contract: each capability is declared as supported or not; attempting all three against a real store yields a definite result for each, and a declaration that does not match what the store did is a failure

criteria.condition: an operation needs a capability the store does not have
criteria.action: fail the operation with an answer naming the missing capability
criteria.contract: the error message names the capability; the operation does not fall back to a different effect, and the repository is left as it was

criteria.action: behave as its capability report says for each of the three capabilities
criteria.contract: for each capability reported as supported, the operation succeeds against a real store; for each reported as unsupported, it fails

requirements.title: Size
requirements.rationale: The store caps a repository, and an operation that silently truncates or hangs at the cap is worse than one that refuses.

criteria.action: copy in, read and write a repository holding at most 500 MB of packed objects and at most 10000 refs, those figures standing until they are measured against a real store
criteria.contract: a repository at both limits reaches status ready and its refs are all readable afterwards; where the fixture cannot be built the check skips with a reason naming what is missing, and the measured ceilings replace these figures

criteria.condition: an operation would take a repository past what the store accepts
criteria.action: fail it with the route's documented storage-failure answer, from its own accounting of what it has written, and leave the workspace usable
criteria.contract: the error message names the 1 GB repository limit; the workspace is still readable and its earlier refs are unchanged

requirements.title: Resolving a workspace's git credential
requirements.rationale: Every remote operation in every later package reads this, so a wrong fallback order sends the wrong credential to the wrong host.

criteria.action: resolve the origin credential as GIT_PAT, else GIT_USERNAME with GIT_PASSWORD, else none
criteria.contract: with both GIT_PAT and the basic pair present the token is used; with only the pair the pair is used; with neither no credential is sent

criteria.action: resolve the upstream credential as UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT, else UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME with UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD, else the origin credential
criteria.contract: with no upstream secret at all the origin credential is used for the upstream; with an upstream token present it is used instead

criteria.condition: only one half of a basic credential pair is stored
criteria.action: ignore the half that is present, treat the pair as absent and record that it was ignored
criteria.contract: the resolution falls through to the next option as though neither half existed; a log record says the half pair was ignored and does not contain its value

criteria.action: read the reserved credential names only from the workspace's own scope
criteria.contract: a secret of the same name at the owner's user scope or the workspace's organization scope is not used, and the resolution behaves as though it did not exist

requirements.title: Retiring a repository
requirements.rationale: Branches pushed to Parley exist only there, so releasing a repository without first offering them to the remote loses commits.

criteria.guard: its status is ready and a usable origin credential exists
criteria.action: push every branch of its repository to origin without forcing, and then release the repository
criteria.contract: each branch present only in the workspace's repository, and accepted by origin, exists on origin afterwards; no ref on origin is rewritten; the repository is released from the store

criteria.condition: origin refuses any branch of the archive push, the push fails, or the workspace has no usable origin credential
criteria.action: archive the workspace anyway and keep its repository
criteria.contract: the workspace's status is "archived" and the repository is still in the store with every commit; reactivating it reuses that repository

criteria.action: remove its repository from the store
criteria.contract: the store holds no repository under that workspace's derived name afterwards

requirements.title: The repository store interface
requirements.rationale: This is the one place Cloudflare Artifacts is reached, and the token it issues must never leave the deployment.

criteria.action: reach the repository store only through its platform interface, whose vocabulary is refs and packs rather than any store's SDK, with a Cloudflare implementation over Artifacts and a non-Cloudflare one
criteria.contract: one contract suite exists for the interface and passes against both implementations, as the platform interfaces of package 01 do

criteria.action: keep every store credential inside the deployment
criteria.contract: no response body and no log record contains a repo-scoped store token; a token the service mints for its own use is never returned to a caller

execution_paths.title: A private repository is registered and copied in

steps.action: creates a workspace for a private remote, supplying a git_pat
checks the credential against the remote before writing anything
writes the workspace at pending, creates its repository in the store and queues the copy
copies the refs of the remote into the repository with the stored credential, in batches it can resume, moving the status through cloning
holds the refs and objects durably
polls the workspace and finds status ready with head_sha set

execution_paths.title: A copy fails and the workspace records why

steps.action: creates a workspace for a remote that is reachable at create time but fails during the copy
answers 201 with status pending and begins the copy
fails the copy and sets the workspace to failed with clone_error naming the failure
reads the workspace and sees status failed and clone_error, with no credential in the message

execution_paths.title: A repository is pushed out, released and finally removed

steps.action: archives a ready workspace holding a branch that exists nowhere else
resolves the origin credential from the workspace's secrets and pushes every branch to origin without forcing
releases the repository and answers with status archived
no longer holds a repository for that workspace
